summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, systolic heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for abdominal pain found to be due to a distal SMA thrombus with possible bowel ischemia. He was on a heparin drip and NPO status when he suddenly developed left-sided weakness and dysarthria. Imaging revealed a complete occlusion of the right internal carotid artery and right MCA, leading to a large right MCA stroke. He underwent unsuccessful mechanical thrombectomy and was intubated due to agitation. He was managed in the neuro ICU for cerebral edema risk, developed transient anisocoria requiring mannitol, and was treated for presumed aspiration pneumonia with antibiotics. His fluid and electrolyte balance was carefully managed, including correction of hypernatremia. He gradually improved, passed a swallow study, and was restarted on warfarin. He was discharged to extended care with stable neurologic status, safe for ground solids and thickened liquids, and plans for rehabilitation and close follow-up.
